VERTEX-CRITICAL FOUR-CHROMATIC GRAPHS
WITH NO SMALL CRITICAL EDGE SET
LIAM KRUER AND JENSEN KOHLMEYER
ABSTRACT. We construct, for every positive integer 𝑟, a finite four-chromatic graph whose every vertex is
critical, while deleting any set of at most𝑟 edges leaves its chromatic number unchanged. The construction
combines punctured cyclic three-colorings, an integral height character, an Andrasfai winding inequality,
and a Chinese remainder construction with an exact classification of its small-deficit characters. Together
with the established result of Skottova and Steiner for five or more colors, this gives an affirmative answer
to the existence statement in Erdős problem 944. The complete existence statement for all 𝑘 ≥ 4 is
formalized in one Lean file with 570 proved theorems. This includes the four-color parameter construction
and character argument, and the higher-color construction, local structure, and propagation proof. The
exact challenge theorem is checked without admitted proof placeholders or additional axioms.
1. INTRODUCTION
An edge set of a graph is critical if deleting it lowers the chromatic number. A graph is vertex-
critical if deleting any vertex lowers its chromatic number. We use the terminology (𝑘, 𝑟 )-graph for a
finite graph 𝐺 satisfying
𝜒(𝐺) = 𝑘, 𝜒 (𝐺 − 𝑣) = 𝑘 − 1 (𝑣 ∈ 𝑉 (𝐺)), 𝜒 (𝐺 − 𝐸 ′) = 𝑘 (𝐸 ′ ⊆ 𝐸 (𝐺), | 𝐸 ′| ≤ 𝑟). (1)
The existence statement of Erdős problem 944 asks whether a (𝑘, 𝑟 )-graph exists for every 𝑘 ≥ 4 and 𝑟 ≥
1; it is also the statement selected by the Formal Conjectures challenge [ 2, 3]. Skottova and Steiner [ 1,
Theorem 1.3] prove the existence of such graphs for every 𝑘 ≥ 5 and 𝑟 ≥ 1. Their result leaves the
four-color case.
Theorem 1.1 (Construction) . For every integer 𝑟 ≥ 1, there is a finite (4, 𝑟)-graph.
Corollary 1.2. For every 𝑘 ≥ 4 and 𝑟 ≥ 1, there is a finite (𝑘, 𝑟 )-graph.
The corollary combines Theorem 1.1 with the cited higher-color theorem. We do not claim a bound
of practical size for the number of vertices, nor the stronger assertion about the existence of graphs of
every sufficiently large order.
